prompt.brief: Design text snippets with generated URLs, expiration, and sharing so users can create and retrieve a paste reliably at scale.
successSignals: Define the source of truth for paste content and ownership and make retries idempotent.
Use bounded, partitioned state to meet 10M pastes per day and 100K reads per second and p95 <=100ms reads.
Separate the critical request path from expiration cleanup, abuse scanning, and analytics.
Explain consistency, failure recovery, authorization, observability, and a degraded mode.

functional: Support the core workflow to create and retrieve a paste.
Expose status, results, and freshness appropriate to text snippets with generated URLs, expiration, and sharing.
Support authorization, validation, updates, deletion, and recovery semantics.
nonFunctional: Meet p95 <=100ms reads under normal load.
Scale to 10M pastes per day and 100K reads per second without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 10M pastes per day and 100K reads per second
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

apis.contract: { content, visibility, expiresAt, password?, idempotencyKey } -> { pasteId, alias, status }
apis.notes: Validate size, retention, content policy, and ownership before storing the paste.
Resolve a short alias with expiry and access checks on every miss.
Allow only authorized policy changes and invalidate cached reads.
Write a tombstone and asynchronously remove content replicas and search/abuse indexes.

dataFlow.title: Create and validate a paste
dataFlow.description: The API checks size, expiry, visibility, abuse policy, and idempotency, then stores content and alias metadata durably.

dataFlow.title: Resolve a short alias
dataFlow.description: Edge and cache look up the alias; cache misses read metadata and content, recheck expiry and access policy, and return a bounded response.

dataFlow.title: Scan and moderate asynchronously
dataFlow.description: A queue sends content to secret, malware, and abuse scanners; a policy result can hide a paste without deleting audit evidence.

dataFlow.title: Expire and delete safely
dataFlow.description: Expiry workers write tombstones, evict aliases, and delete content by lifecycle policy while preserving ownership and deletion audit.

dataFlow.title: Measure reads without hurting redirects
dataFlow.description: Click/read events leave the serving path and are aggregated asynchronously with privacy and retention controls.

architecture.title: Pastebin reference architecture
architecture.summary: A small durable metadata service controls immutable paste bodies, while cache and CDN layers absorb read traffic and event workers handle lifecycle and moderation.

deepDives.title: Alias resolution and cache safety
points: For the Pastebin-like paste service, an alias must never resolve to expired, deleted, or unauthorized content.
Design for the failure case where a hot alias, abuse burst, or cleanup lag must not expose content or take down reads; keep retries, versions, and repair state explicit.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

deepDives.title: Expiry, deletion, and lifecycle
points: For the Pastebin-like paste service, an alias must never resolve to expired, deleted, or unauthorized content.
Keep this concern off unrelated request paths and partition it by the Pastebin-like paste service access key.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

tradeoffs.title: Mutable paste versus immutable versions
tradeoffs.recommendation: Prefer immutable content versions and an explicit latest pointer when editing is required.
tradeoffs.caution: In-place edits complicate cache invalidation, audit, and link consistency.

tradeoffs.title: Synchronous scan versus fast creation
tradeoffs.recommendation: Accept within size/policy limits and quarantine or label content while deep scanning asynchronously.
tradeoffs.caution: Blocking every create on scanners raises tail latency and couples availability to third parties.

tradeoffs.title: Long cache TTL versus revocation
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use short policy-aware TTLs and targeted invalidation for password, delete, and abuse changes.
tradeoffs.caution: A long TTL improves hot reads but can serve revoked or expired content.

commonMistakes: Caching private or expired pastes under an alias-only key.
Generating aliases without collision and idempotency handling.
Deleting content without tombstoning aliases and replicas.
Running unbounded scanners on the create or read path.
Collecting raw paste content in analytics logs.

followUps.question: What if a paste becomes abusive after it is cached?
followUps.answer: Mark it blocked in the policy store, invalidate the alias cache, and let reads recheck policy before serving stale content.

followUps.question: How do you handle an alias hot spot?
followUps.answer: Use edge caching with policy-aware keys, rate limits, and origin shielding while keeping invalidation targeted.

followUps.question: How do you guarantee expiry?
followUps.answer: Store expiry with the alias, reject it on every origin read, and use asynchronous deletion only as physical cleanup.

rubric.description: The answer defines short-link resolution, privacy, expiry, deletion, abuse quarantine, cache invalidation, and bounded content handling, scale, latency, durability, authorization, and failure behavior.
Entities and keys make the Pastebin-like paste service state, versions, lifecycle, and derived projections explicit.
Partitioning, queues, backpressure, cache behavior, hot-key handling, and bounded work are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded behavior, observability, and auditability protect the primary contract.
The candidate can explain the Pastebin-like paste service consistency boundary, asynchronous work, and operational limits.
